radiology_report:
Amsterdam UMC VUmc | 15 January 2025 | Prostate Multiparametric MRI

Clinical indication:
A 76-year-old gentleman presents for targeted assessment following a prior negative biopsy and an elevated prostate-specific antigen reading of 5.8 ng/mL.

FINDINGS:
Prostatic dimensions total 39.0 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a 12 mm hypointense focus located in the right posterior peripheral zone at the mid-gland. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction, mirrored by low ADC signal. Post-contrast phases capture early, focal enhancement against the background parenchyma. The capsular margins remain intact without extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle involvement, and no suspicious lymph nodes are visualized.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 39.0 mL; PSA density 0.15 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.40801913.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: June 2024 laboratory data showed a prostate-specific antigen level of 5.9 ng/mL, which has since stabilized at 5.8 ng/mL on repeat analysis. The sustained elevation alongside a previously negative biopsy prompted a urology referral for deeper assessment.
